origin.description: Write a zoo series to a text file by adding the index column and calling write.table.
origin.usage:
write.zoo(x, file = "", index.name = "Index", row.names = FALSE, col.names = NULL,
  FUN = format, ...)

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: File or connection to write. An empty string writes to standard output.

arguments.name: index.name
arguments.text: Name of the index column. It must not already be a column name. The default is Index.

arguments.name: row.names
arguments.text: Whether to write row names. The default is FALSE because the row names only repeat the index.

arguments.name: col.names
arguments.text: Whether to write column names. The default writes them only when x has column names.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Function that formats the index before it is written. The default is format.
Further arguments passed to write.table, such as sep, dec, and quote.

origin.details: write.zoo coerces the series to a data frame, formats the index, moves that column to the front, and calls write.table. Character columns, including the formatted index, are quoted. Numeric data are written with as.character rules: 15 significant digits, and scientific notation when it is shorter.
origin.value: Invisible NULL. The file text is the result that is compared.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(zoo))
z <- zoo(cbind(a = c(1.5, 3.5, 5.25), b = c(2.25, 4.75, 6.125)), c(1, 2, 3))
path <- tempfile()
write.zoo(z, path)
cat(readChar(path, file.info(path)$size))

translation.description: write_zoo formats the index and writes a table whose first column is that index.
translation.usage:
write_zoo(x, file="", index_name="Index", row_names=False, col_names=None,
  FUN=None, **kwargs)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Zoo. Column names are the columns attribute. A 1-d series has no column names.

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path to write. An empty string writes to standard output.

arguments.name: index_name
arguments.text: Header of the index column. The default is Index, and it must not match a data column.

arguments.name: row_names
arguments.text: Whether to write row names. The default is False.

arguments.name: col_names
arguments.text: Whether to write a header. None writes a header only when x.columns is set.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Formats the whole index. None uses R's format: dates as YYYY-MM-DD and equal-width integers padded on the left.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Passed to the table writer: sep, eol, na, dec, quote, append, and qmethod.

translation.details: The index is formatted first, so format(c(1, 2, 3)) is "1", "2", "3" and those cells are quoted. Numeric cells use 15 significant digits and scientific notation when that form is shorter. The header is quoted and the separator is a space.
translation.value: None. The written text matches write.zoo for the same series.
translation.example:
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/ahmed/killr_projects/killr/packages/zoo")
from zoo.io import write_zoo
from zoo.series import Zoo

z = Zoo(
    np.array([[1.5, 2.25], [3.5, 4.75], [5.25, 6.125]], dtype=float),
    np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]),
)
z.columns = ["a", "b"]
path = tempfile.mktemp()
write_zoo(z, path)
sys.stdout.write(Path(path).read_text())
